choices.why: Perfect participle with ἤδη conveys imminent fulfillment; 'already upon us' captures the temporal urgency better than 'existing now' or 'present'
rejected: the existing time
the present time
the time now at hand

choices.english: Christ has made his dwelling in us
choices.why: Aorist active indicates completed action; 'made his dwelling' is idiomatic for κατῴκηκεν in theological context, more natural than 'dwelt' or 'resided'
rejected: Christ dwelt in us
Christ has dwelt in us
Christ resides in us

choices.term: ἵν' ἡμᾶς ἀποφήνῃ ναοὺς Θεοῦ ζῶντος
choices.english: in order to declare us temples of the living God
choices.why: ἵνα with subjunctive expresses purpose; 'declare us' preserves the causative force of ἀποφήνῃ better than 'make us' or 'show us to be'
rejected: to show us as temples
to make us temples
that we may be declared temples

choices.term: κολλώμενος τῷ Κυρίῳ ἓν πνεῦμά ἐστι
choices.english: whoever is united to the Lord is one spirit with him
choices.why: Middle participle κολλώμενος implies mutual joining; 'united to' captures the reciprocal sense better than 'joined' or 'clinging to'
rejected: who is joined to the Lord
the one clinging to the Lord
he who binds himself to the Lord

choices.term: Οὐ περὶ τούτων δὲ ἐρωτῶ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων
choices.english: I ask not only for these, but also for all who will believe
choices.why: Περί with accusative indicates object of request; 'ask for' is natural for ἐρωτῶ in intercessory context, more accurate than 'pray concerning' or 'request about'
rejected: I do not ask only concerning these but also concerning all
I request not only for these but also for all
My prayer is not only for these but also for all

choices.english: the glory you have given me
choices.why: Perfect active indicative δέδωκας emphasizes completed gift; 'you have given me' preserves the perfect aspect better than 'you gave' or 'which you bestowed'
rejected: the glory which you gave me
the glory you have bestowed upon me
the glory that was given to me by you

choices.why: Aorist active indicates historical incarnation; 'tabernacled' is literal for ἐσκήνωσεν and preserves the Exodus/Shekinah allusion better than 'dwelled' or 'lived'
rejected: dwelled among us
lived among us
made his home among us

choices.term: Υἱὸς εἷς καὶ Κύριος εἷς Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστός
choices.english: One Son and One Lord, Jesus Christ
choices.why: Appositional structure with repeated εἷς emphasizes unity; 'One Son and One Lord' preserves the emphatic word order better than 'Jesus Christ, who is both one Son and one Lord'
rejected: Jesus Christ is one Son and one Lord
One Son, one Lord—Jesus Christ
the one Son and the one Lord, Jesus Christ

pass_b_english: Since the time had now come for this promise to be fulfilled, Christ took up his dwelling in us according to the ancient pledge, so that he might declare us to be temples of the living God—indeed, temples of himself—and might unite us to God the Father through himself.
He said to his holy apostles, 'On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you are in me, and I am in you.' (John 14:20)
For whoever is united to the Lord becomes one spirit with him, as the Scripture declares. (1 Corinthians 6:17)

Again, committing us to God and the Father in this same way, he said, 'I do not pray for these alone, but also for all who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I am in you, so that they too may be one in us, in order that the world may believe that you sent me.' (John 17:20-21)
And the glory which you gave me I have given to them, that they may be one as we are one—I in them and you in me—so that they may be brought to complete unity. (John 17:22-23)

Therefore, in Christ we have obtained the blessing of unity toward God and Father, and this blessing remains firmly in us: that radiant and manifest adornment which belongs to those who preserve their boldness and the boast of their hope.
Moreover, in regard to this, they do not believe that alongside God the Father there exists another son who is distinct and merely partial, the one born of the holy virgin and made a temple.

Instead, they believe that he has come in accordance with the writings—that the Word became flesh and tabernacled among us—and that he has not ceased to be God, but that he is One Son and One Lord, Jesus Christ.
And he scrutinizes even to the point of division.
